title: A pawn on d2 and a knight from board A turn board B
summary: White on board B led for most of the game, helped by the queen that Nxd1 won on board A, while board A swung back and forth. Black on board B turned it with the pawn drop P@d2, a knight sent over by Rxg2 and a new queen on d1, then mated, starting with B@g2+ with a bishop won on board A. Watch Black on board A in the last moves: behind, it keeps its queen and rooks away from White, because each would let Black on board B mate, and it ends by sitting.
event: HypeBeast 1.1.1 against HypeBeast 1.1.0, 500,000 nodes a move

result.text: Black on board B mates; the team of A-White and B-Black wins.

moves.note: Taking the knight sends it to Black on board B, who later dropped it as N@f5. Most of the engine's high score was what captured pieces would be worth on board B; on board A alone it counted itself behind. By its next move it scored itself about three pawns down, and a longer search would have dropped P@c4 first. It expected a pawn from board B, and Nxg2 there sent one.

lines.note: The engine's plan, which the game followed: P@d3 with the expected pawn, then Bxd3.
A search that ignores the other board plays Bg5 first, and scored it far above the capture searched the same way.
A longer search drops P@c4 first and takes on c6 only after dxc4, which it scored much higher.
At its next turn Black's engine already scored the position in its own favour, planning knight drops on h4 and f3.
With the expected pawn in hand the engine still chose Bxc6+, and a fresh search of the reply scored White about four pawns down.

moves.note: This is the pawn that Nxg2 on board B had just sent over, as the engine expected when it played Bxc6+. Its first choice was P@b7, but it thought Black might get a bishop from board B, and in that case it rated P@d3 well ahead. Its next move took back with Bxd3, as its plan had said.

White expected a pawn for itself and a bishop for Black from board A, and both came, with Bxb7 and Nxb7 there. In that case it rated Ne4 slightly higher, but over all cases Bg5 and Ne4 were nearly level. By its next turn, after Black's P@h4, White's own score had turned from about seven pawns up to about six down, and nothing in its lines shows why.

lines.note: White's own plan after Bg5, with Ne4 and P@h5 to follow.
Black's plan at its next turn began with P@f6 and still left White well ahead, so it does not explain the fall; Black played P@h4 instead.

moves.note: Its first choice was Nxb7, taking a pawn. But it expected its partner on board A to win a knight (about seven chances in ten), and with a knight in hand it rated Nxh3, taking the bishop, far higher. gxh3 there did win the knight, and by Black's next move its score had turned in its favour. The bishop went to White on board A, who later dropped it on b7.

lines.note: White's answer by a fresh search: exd8=Q, as in the game.
The first choice Nxb7 and the engine's line after it, which White answers with exf8=N.
With the knight in hand the engine planned N@g3+ after Qxh3.

moves.note: The bishop is the one Nxh3 won on board B. White drops it on b7 expecting a queen from board B (it gave that nearly one chance in two), and on the very next move Bxf2 there took the queen of White on board B and sent it over. On its next move this bishop took on c6 with check, and White's engine scored about 25 pawns in its favour.

On its previous move Black's first choice N@h3 had been replaced by B@g1, next to White's queen on f2. Now the bishop takes the queen, which goes to White on board A, who drops it with Q@g4 soon after.

Three moves after N@e3+, the knight takes White's queen on d1. The queen goes to White on board B, who drops it with check on its next move, Q@g8+, and Rxd1 sends the knight to Black on board B, who blocks that check with it, N@f8.

This is the queen that Nxd1 had just won on board A; when it played Bxg3 on its previous move, White's engine already thought a queen would very probably come. It drops it at once with check. Black blocks with N@f8, using the knight that Rxd1 had just sent from board A.

lines.note: White's own line after the block N@f8, with Qxg7 to come.
A search that ignores the other board plays P@a7, which the same method scored well below Q@g8+.
Black's plan at its next turn, N@f8 and then B@g6+, still left White well ahead by Black's own count.

moves.note: Its first choice was Qd2. It expected its partner to win a knight on board A (about seven chances in ten), and with a knight in hand it rated the pawn drop on d2 far above the queen move. The knight came with Rxg2, Black dropped it on c1 beside the pawn, and the pawn queened with check two moves later. From here board B turned Black's way.

lines.note: White's answer by a fresh search, N@d3, as in the game; it still left Black far behind.
After the first choice Qd2 the engine's line has White promoting on a8 with check.

moves.note: The pawn dropped with P@d2 queens with check, with the knight that Rxg2 sent from board A standing on c1. At P@d2 Black's engine counted itself about twelve pawns down; here it counts itself about three pawns up, and board B stays Black's to the end.

On board A alone Black counted itself ahead, but after its first choice P@h3, Qxd7+ Qxd7 Nxd7 lets White's knight take Black's queen, and by its count a queen in the hand of Black on board B was enough to mate there. So it took the rook on g2 with check, sending the rook to its partner. After Rxg2 the bishop went the other way: Black on board B later dropped it with B@g2+ to start the mate.

lines.note: White's answer by a fresh search, Kxg2; in the game it took back with the rook, Rxg2, and that sent the bishop to board B.
The first choice P@h3: after Qxd7+ Qxd7 Nxd7 Black's queen goes to board B.
A search that ignores the other board plays P@f5, which the same method scored a little below Bxg2+.
With the expected pawn in hand the plan was the one played: Rxg2, then P@f3.

moves.note: This is the pawn that Kxg2 on board B had just sent, as Black expected. It also expected White on board A to receive a rook from board B, and even then it rated P@f3 its best try. The rook came with Qxe2+, and by its next move Black's own score was far worse. A longer search preferred Be4, but only by a little: no line here holds.

lines.note: Its own line still lets White trade queens with Qxd7+ and take Black's queen with Nxd7.
A search that ignores the other board plays Bh5, which the same method scored below P@f3.
A longer search prefers Be4, scored only a little above P@f3.
White took the pawn with Rxf3, as in the game; its plan goes on to promote with bxa8=Q.

moves.note: Its first choice P@h3 again allowed Qxd7+ and the queen trade that gives Black on board B a queen. It expected a queen of its own from board B, with a knight going to White, and with that queen in hand it rated the pawn drop on f2 clearly higher. Both came on the next two moves, with Nxe2 and Nxe1+, but by then Black on board B had a forced mate by its own count. Black here was lost either way.

lines.note: White's answer by a fresh search, Rfxf2, as in the game.
The first choice P@h3: White trades queens on d7 and its knight takes Black's queen.
A search that ignores the other board plays Bh5, which the same method scored a little above P@f2.

moves.note: The bishop is the one White won with Rxg2 on board A, after Black there had taken the rook on g2. B@g2+ starts a mate in three by the engine's count; B@f1+ also mated, one move slower. White's moves from here were forced.

lines.note: The engine's line ends with P@g6+; in the game Nf6# came instead.

moves.note: Its first choice was to drop the queen that Nxe2 had sent from board B, Q@b1. But then bxa8=Q takes the rook on a8, and Black on board B could drop that rook with R@h3+ for mate. So the rook steps to b8. After P@a7 Black on board A sat for the rest of the game: by its count every move let White send Black on board B a piece to mate with, such as the a6 pawn taken by the knight and dropped on g6.

lines.note: White's answer by a fresh search, P@a7, as in the game.
The first choice Q@b1, after which the engine's own line has White taking the rook with bxa8=Q.

moves.note: The knight reached e1 with Nxe1+ on move 51. Now it checks from f3, Kh5 is White's only move, and the other knight mates on f6.

lines.note: The engine's line gives P@g6+ after Kh5; in the game Nf6# was mate at once.

moves.note: Mate. Black on board A had sat since White's P@a7, so as not to hand over the pawn that would let this side mate with a drop on g6; the mate came on f6 instead. White on board A was well ahead there by its own count, but the game ends on board B.
